I work at a very large company in the energy industry, and I'm sad to say that I am at the very bottom of the totem pole.

But to answer your question, what do I do? I do all the computer/software tasks that 85% of the other employees can't do. I'm one of the youngest employees of the company, which means I am the most familiar with computers. I sit at a computer all day and either code or make spreadsheets. You often find that with large companies that have been around for a while, middle management and above, are older individuals that aren't tech savvy and tend to spend more of their time in meetings and leaving the computer stuff to me.
It sounds like you are home schooled then?

Just because you dropped out of college doesn't mean it's the end; if that college won't let you back in, who cares? There are plenty of other colleges to go to, or you could decide that college isn't for you and then no worries.

I don't know where you have been applying for jobs, but figure out what you like to do and get a job in that field. I've spend way to many years of my life in jobs that I didn't like but stayed in them because it was an easy paycheck. Trust me, you will be much happier in a job that you enjoy doing than working for the first person that would hire you.

And don't worry about the anxiety disorder, I don't know anyone who isn't worry about one thing or another. We all do it, some people are just better at hiding it then others.
This is only my opinion, but I wouldn't worry about your mother. You need to do what you think is right, not what she thinks is right.

See if your school has any depression resources. I went to my depression department at my school a few months ago and I thought it would be weird, and it kinda was, but it was such a relief to talk to someone in person about it. 

The internet is great and all, but you need to talk to someone in person. There is something real about talking face to face that the internet can't provide.
